messages.author: c6faebb940c11bea
messages.subject: A question about lm.rrpp?
parts:
Hello,

In the vignette using RRPP, second example demonstrates:

data(Pupfish)
Pupfish$logSize <- log(Pupfish$CS) 
fit <- lm.rrpp(coords ~ logSize + Sex*Pop, SS.type = "I", 
               data = Pupfish, print.progress = FALSE) 
summary(fit, formula = FALSE)

And it is said: "ANOVA results reveal that after accounting for body size allometry, not only are there significant inter-population differences in body shape and sexual dimorphism in body shape, but sexual dimorphism also 
significantly varies between the two populations. "

How is this function accounting for allometry here?


Thanks,

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] A question about lm.rrpp?
parts:
Burak,

allometry being the relationship between shape and size, in this example allometric variation is being accounted for by including logSize (the logarithm of CS) as the first term in the linear model being fitted.

Antigoni

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] A question about lm.rrpp?
parts:
Thank you Antigoni,

What I am confused about is the difference from geomorph vignette. In geomorph vignette two models are used for this purpose a null model and a full model e.g.

pup.null <- procD.lm(coords ~ logSize + Sex + Pop, data = Pupfish, print.progress = FALSE)
pup.full <- procD.lm(coords ~ logSize + Sex * Pop, data = Pupfish, print.progress = FALSE)

And then anova or pairwise functions are used to test the difference after accounting for allometry. A similar approach was used in the old version with advanced.procD.lm. Here in the rrpp only the full model is used as an input. If I am not wrong, method in the geomorph only tests for the interaction term. Then is there an advantage of one approach over the other? What would be the model to use with lm.rrpp if I wanted to account for both common allometry and sex (I am asking this to compare with the example in the geomorph package)?

I have been reading the papers and the help pages and I am a bit confused with all the different functions seemingly doing the same thing actually.

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] A question about lm.rrpp?
parts:
Burak,

I´m not sure it is useful to compare examples across packages. Although the authors are (in this case) the same, the purpose of help files is different.

In the example from the geomorph vignette, yes, the term being tested by comparing those two models is the interaction between sex:pop.

The example of RRPP, is illustrating how one might use the lm.rrpp function to evaluate the contribution of sex, population, and their interaction, while accounting for allometry.

Keep in mind that people that use RRPP do not necessarily also use geomorph (but not the other way around, as in reality procD.lm is a wrapper for lm.rrpp). So examples are built with different motivations and purposes. Not sure there is something to understand or compare here.

Hope this helps

Antigoni
